key_insight: TDAL learns how to choose the next perturbation online, rather than relying on a fixed acquisition rule, so the selection strategy can adapt as screening feedback accumulates.
clinical_relevance: More adaptive perturbation screening could help prioritize the most informative genetic or drug targets sooner, potentially improving discovery efficiency in therapeutic research.
method: Frames budgeted perturbation discovery as a sequential decision problem.
Uses temporal difference learning to update the acquisition function from a single screening trajectory.
Applies Hellinger distance and leave-batch-out replay to estimate future value and expand training signals.
evidence_signal: Across eight public perturbation screens covering single, double, and triple perturbations, TDAL averaged rank 1.63 among 11 methods and ranked first on four tasks.
watch_item: Because TDAL learns from prior screening trajectories and virtual transitions, performance may depend on how well the training screens match the new experimental setting.
paper_title: Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery
